key_insight: VIME uses classical imaginary-time pre-training with a compressed ansatz to prepare molecular ground states with much lower quantum circuit cost than prior Majorana-evolution baselines.
engineering_relevance: It offers a path to hardware-efficient, early fault-tolerant quantum chemistry by reducing CNOT count, two-qubit depth, and state-preparation overhead.
method: Extends OVQITE to molecular electronic structure via a single compiled Majorana-propagation surrogate graph.
Pairs the pre-training with a compressed tiled Unitary Product State (c-tUPS) ansatz to shrink simulation and preparation costs.
Targets strongly correlated, multireference molecules with resource-efficient ground-state preparation.
evidence_signal: On TLD-1411, active-space calculations up to 52 qubits reached chemical precision against DMRG, with errors about 400× smaller than ADAPT-VQE-based VMPE; across acenes up to heptacene (60 qubits), VIME matched or improved accuracy with up to 26× fewer CNOTs and 167× lower two-qubit depth.
watch_item: The approach relies on classical pre-training and compiled surrogate graphs, so performance may depend on problem structure, ansatz compression quality, and accurate mapping to hardware-efficient circuits.
paper_title: Hardware-Efficient Ground-State Preparation using Variational Imaginary-Time Majorana Evolution
